name: Motorola MT4310
summary: Motorola MT4310 (Argentina) ships with store demo, silent installs and promo rows. TidyTV is a free phone app that turns them off, with a backup and undo.
intro: This 43-inch Motorola set, sold in Argentina, runs Android TV 11 and has under 1 GB of memory. It ships with silent installers, a store demo, setup leftovers, telemetry, recommendation and promo rows, and a few unused system services. It is a small set, so memory is tight.

It was done in batches on one TV with a home screen check after each, then a restart. Live TV, HDMI switching and the real remote's buttons were checked. TidyTV turns these off from your phone over Wi-Fi, saves a backup first and never deletes anything. It had held up for a day when it was written.
keep: Live TV, HDMI and the Input key (MediaTek TV service)
The remote's YouTube, Prime Video and Disney+ keys
The setup helper, which does not take over Home here
notes: The TV's factory tool turns Google Assistant and the recommendation service back on at every start, so they are not on the list.
The screen sleeps after 5 minutes idle and Wi-Fi drops with it. If the TV seems to vanish after a restart, press Power.
The remote's mic button opens Bluetooth pairing until the remote is paired.
Never open the factory menus on this TV, even to look.

faq.q: Do the Netflix and YouTube buttons still work?
faq.a: Yes. The TV's own key services handle them, so they keep working with a new home screen.

faq.q: Why are Assistant and recommendations still on?
faq.a: The TV's factory tool turns them back on at every start, so the list does not try to switch them off.

faq.q: Does it have a way back?
faq.a: Yes. Restore everything in the app turns every app back on in one tap, and puts the old home screen back if you changed it.
